gap.why: Personality turned 14.8% of 29,520 daily-activity picks at the general trait weight of 1. Studies of extraversion and time spent socializing (Mehl et al. 2006) report no extractable coefficient, so the general weight stands.
gap.fix: Calibrate when a study gives a size for extraversion and social time.

gap.why: Personality turned none of 1,471 drive responses in Ely, Nevada at any weight up to 8: the drive's own strength separates the options. No study gives a size (neuroticism and rumination is the direction).
gap.fix: None until the options score closer or a study gives a size; the general trait weight of 1 stands.

gap.why: No study of owners' draws by personality has a number, so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study). An owner weighs the business's cash against a month of everything it pays out, not only payroll, so 40 to 50 percent of weighings sit within a point of keeping, and temperament turns some of them.
gap.fix: A study that reports owners' withdrawals by trait.

gap.why: Owners never open a second location in 282 weighings: the expand score sits 6 to 9 below keeping (baseline -3, room term, src/core2/modules/business.ts:1551), and no study of owners' expansion by personality has a number.
gap.fix: Find a study of owner expansion and calibrate the expand baseline against it.

gap.why: Zimmerman 2008 (Personnel Psychology 61(2), a meta-analysis of personality and turnover) gives only the direction in the text read (conscientiousness and agreeableness best predict actual turnover), so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study number); a fit to an assumed 1.2 per standard deviation is not used.
gap.fix: Read the per-trait sizes from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-turnover-zimmerman-per-trait).

gap.fix: Read the per-trait sizes from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-turnover-zimmerman-per-trait).

gap.why: Runs on an election day; most places hold none in the default audit year. With TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1 it ran 594 times in Halfway, Missouri (2929962, seed 3e9ed70a5fb7, December 3, 2025 to December 3, 2026) and 1,349 in Marblehead, Ohio (3947502, seed 7772ab1c8196, January 20, 2025 to January 20, 2026) (2,681 in Parkway, Missouri, seed e6ff0d60d6bc). Its weight (0.79) is cited to Mondak et al. 2010 (odds ratio 1.98): net odds 2.12 in Halfway and 3.77 in Marblehead.
gap.fix: Audit the place's own election window (TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1); Marblehead's high odds stay open under traits-wire-civic.

gap.why: Runs where a race with an incumbent falls in the played year (TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1): 3,413 appeals in Halfway, Missouri (2929962, seed 3e9ed70a5fb7, December 3, 2025 to December 3, 2026) and 4,712 in Marblehead, Ohio (3947502, seed 7772ab1c8196, January 20, 2025 to January 20, 2026). No study gives a size, so the general weight of 1 stands. In Halfway the third leaning most toward the incumbent backs them 0.71 of the time and the third leaning least 0.64 (flat 0.50 and 0.59), net 1.98; in Marblehead 1.00 and 0.79 (flat 0.92 and 0.93), net about 378.
gap.fix: Calibrate when a study gives the size, at the single-decision range meanwhile (traits-wire-civic).

gap.why: standsAgain (src/core2/modules/voting.ts:319) is read only from fileStandingCandidates (:1126), which returns at :1132 whenever the candidacy module is installed, and candidacy owns every incumbent's decision to run or stay out (its own decision, candidacy.run). Every played world installs candidacy, so the call at :1196 is never reached, in the election window as in the default year.
gap.fix: Fold the age term (standAgainReason, voting.ts:334) into candidacy's reasons for an incumbent and delete standsAgain and the stand-in branch, or measure the decision only in a world built without candidacy (pool item elections-stand-again-dead-with-candidacy).

gap.why: Runs on a measure's election date, so only in an election-window year (TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1): 123 voters weighed it in Halfway, Missouri (2929962, seed 3e9ed70a5fb7, December 3, 2025 to December 3, 2026), none in Marblehead, Ohio (3947502, seed 7772ab1c8196, January 20, 2025 to January 20, 2026), whose calendar holds no measure that year; main's audit found 277 in Parkway, Missouri (seed e6ff0d60d6bc). No study gives a size, so the general weight of 1 stands, and at weight 1 the trait term settles the vote: in Halfway the third leaning most toward change backed the measure 0.80 of the time and the third leaning least 0.00 (flat 0.78 and 0.61), net odds about 148.
gap.fix: Weigh more of the voter's own circumstances than their view of the question, then calibrate to a cited size (traits-wire-civic).
